https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/22/magy.text: Menü Kereső Elkezdték visszakapcsolni a Paksi Atomerőmű harmadik turbináját FRISSÜL Belföld Nagy Nikoletta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Cikkünk folyamatosan frissül! Jelenleg két turbina működik Pakson, a mai nap egy harmadikat, a 3-as blokk 6-os turbináját is felkapcsolják, és mostantól kezdve folyamatosan állítják vissza a teljesítményt az atomerőműben, mondta el Magyar Péter egy Facebook-videóban . Azt is mondta, hogy az erőmű szerdára éri el a végleges teljesítményt, a 2000 megawattot. A folyamat nem most indult, mondta a miniszterelnök, hanem majdnem két napja, ugyanis 49 óráig tart egy turbina visszakapcsolása, ennek az utolsó 3 órájához érkeztünk. Ez a legfontosabb része, ilyenkor kezdődik el a turbina löketése, vagyis a fordulatszám elérése. Vigh Károly, a Paksi Atomerőmű üzemviteli igazgatója azt mondta, hogy a turbina most is 3-4 fordulat per perc sebességgel forog, mert el kell kerülni azt, hogy a turbina tengelye elgörbüljön a gőztől, és egyenletes legyen a hőeloszlás. Az erőmű dolgozói jelenleg végigellenőrzik a gépet, és ha indításra alkalmasnak találják, akkor megkezdődik a turbinában a gőz vezetése. Három szakaszban fogják visszakapcsolni a turbinát, az első szakaszban 600 fordulat per percig növelik a fordulatszámot, ezt már elérték. Ezután ellenőriznek, aztán 900 fordulat per percre, újabb ellenőrzés után pedig végül 3000 fordulat per percre emelik. Az utolsó szakasz a legkritikusabb, itt már 600 fordulat per perccel fogják emelni a sebességet. A mostani várakozások alapján ezután az 1-es blokk 2-es turbinája reggel 5 órától szintén indítható állapotba fog kerülni. Várhatóan holnap reggel 8 órától lehet párhuzamosan kapcsolni majd. Minden évben 6-10 közötti turbinaújraindítást hajtanak végre tervezetten az atomerőműben, így maga a folyamat nem új a szakembereknek. Magyar Péter először július 30-án jelentette be , hogy energia-krízishelyzet jöhet, miután közölte, az aszály és a Duna alacsony vízállása miatt le kell majd állítani a Paksi Atomerőművet, aminek teljesítményét fokozatosan vették vissza a korábbi napokban. Végül a teljes leállításra nem volt szükség többek között az ideiglenes bárkák és az épülő fenékküszöb miatt. Hogy mi az a fenékküszöb, arról ebben a cikkünkben írtunk bővebben . https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: A statement posted simultaneously to Sam Wood and Snezana Wood’s Instagram said it was ‘a difficult time for all of us’. Photograph: Sam Tabone/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A statement posted simultaneously to Sam Wood and Snezana Wood’s Instagram said it was ‘a difficult time for all of us’. Photograph: Sam Tabone/Getty Images Queensland Former Bachelor star Sam Wood charged with domestic violence Police arrested 46-year-old in Noosa and charged him with assault occasioning bodily harm and strangulation in a domestic setting Stephanie Convery Sun 4 Oct 2026 23.17 EDT First published on Sun 4 Oct 2026 20.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The fitness influencer and reality TV star Sam Wood has been charged in Queensland with domestic violence offences. The personal trainer and star of the third season of the Australian version of the reality TV show The Bachelor was charged on Sunday and spent the weekend in police custody after an alleged incident on Saturday night. Mark Watkin, the acting chief executive of 28 Group, now the parent company of the fitness business 28 by Sam Wood, said on Monday that Wood had stepped down from his role indefinitely. “We have all been shocked and saddened by the matters involving Sam Wood,” Watkin said. “We have zero tolerance for domestic violence. While the matter is under investigation and before the court, Sam is on indefinite leave from his duties. “Our thoughts are with the family and anyone in the community affected by domestic violence.” A statement posted simultaneously to Wood’s personal Instagram account and that of his wife, Snezana Wood, on Monday morning, said: “This is a difficult time for all of us, we are working through this as a family and are thoroughly co-operating with authorities.” View image in fullscreen Sam, right, and Snezana Wood, left, both released statements on their Instagram accounts that said they were ‘working through this as a family’. Photograph: Naomi Rahim/WireImage On Sunday Queensland police confirmed they had arrested a 46-year-old Victorian man and charged him with domestic violence offences. The arrest came after officers attended a Noosa address about 9pm on Saturday after receiving reports of alleged domestic violence. ﻿The man had been charged with assaulting occasioning bodily harm (domestic violence) and strangulation in a domestic setting, police said. The alleged victim or victims were not identified. Wood appeared by video-link in Maroochydore magistrates court on Monday. View image in fullscreen Sam and Snezana Wood met in 2015 on the third season of The Bachelor. Photograph: Shine Australia Wood was remanded in custody after the court appearance. His lawyer, Mathew Cuskelly, told AAP that Wood would apply for bail. “He’s simply worried about his family. A bail application will be heard on Thursday,” Cuskelly said. “The charges will be defended.” The personal trainer shot to national prominence when he starred as the eponymous Bachelor in the third season of the reality TV show franchise in 2015. He met Snezana Markoski when she was a contestant on the show. The couple married in 2018 in Byron Bay. They have four daughters, including one from Markoski’s previous relationship. Wood owns and runs the personal training studio The Woodshed in Brighton East, Melbourne. He built a fitness and nutrition business, 28 by Sam Wood, off the back of his increased profile from The Bachelor, eventually selling the company in 2022 for $71.2m. Over the past year, the Australian Taxation Office has been pursuing Wood for alleged unpaid tax debts, reported to be in excess of $7m. Case listings noted in August that a settlement had been reached, with the case dismissed in September. Wood has recently launched a telehealth-based weight-loss platform aimed at middle-aged women, called Ollo for Women. Wood is expected to return to a Queensland court on Thursday. Guardian Australia has approached businesses connected to Wood for comment. https://metro.co.uk/2026/10/17/first-pic.text: Nathan Owens, 34, is said to have strangled Carla Georgescu with a leather belt after driving more than 100 miles through the night to her student halls in Preston (Pictures: Lancashire Police) A man accused of murdering his 19-year-old stepdaughter after developing a ‘dangerous sexual obsession’ with her can be pictured for the first time. Nathan Owens, 34, is said to have strangled Carla Georgescu with a leather belt after driving more than 100 miles through the night to her student halls in Preston in February this year. Jurors have heard Owens kept a secret library of images he had taken of Carla doing household chores in her underwear or pyjamas and had filmed himself having sex with an ‘effigy’ dressed in the teenager’s nightie. His disturbing ‘fascination’ with his stepdaughter may have erupted into a fatal sex attack because he knew Carla was due to fly out to Romania the next day and was planning to meet a new boyfriend, prosecutors said. Footage has already been played at Preston Crown Court showing Carla – wearing a fluffy dressing gown and pyjamas – letting Owens into her accommodation in the early hours of February 4. He is then recorded leaving around 90 minutes later, again with his head and face hidden. Jurors have now seen footage of the moment Owens was arrested at home. Carla’s mum became worried when she failed to reply to messages the following day – what would have been her 20th birthday (Picture: Lancashire Police) To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Up Next Previous Page Next Page After the alleged murder, the court has heard Owens drove back home to Hartlepool, throwing away items including bedding bearing the student’s DNA. Owens’ wife and Carla’s mum, Janina Georgescu, had no idea he left the house and made the journey while she slept, jurors have heard. She later told police her husband would typically stay up all night playing games and usually went to bed when she woke up for work. Mrs Georgescu became worried when Carla failed to reply to messages the following day – what would have been her 20th birthday – and called the police, who found her body. The court heard they initially thought she had taken her own life, before noticing she had several suspicious injuries. Nicholas Lumley KC, prosecuting, has told jurors: ‘Carla Georgescu had been gravely assaulted, beaten about the head, stabbed to the face, the blade connecting with her hands as she tried to defend herself, before being strangled to death by use, at the very least, of the belt and then suspended from the wardrobe handle. ‘There had plainly been some form of grievous sexual activity too. Hardly surprising given his obsession with her.’ Jurors have seen photos of Owens with Carla, including this one of them both looking at their phones over dinner (Picture: Lancashire Police) The court heard Owens’ devices were seized and an examination of them showed he had transferred 14,417 still and moving images to a laptop two weeks before the killing. Most were pornographic but there were also hundreds taken of Carla at the family home, dressed in underwear or short pyjamas, it was said. Owens is also said to have created so-called deepfakes of Carla, superimposing her face onto explicit images. There were also a video and 30 screenshots of Owens having sex with an effigy, wearing Carla’s clothing, jurors heard. Owens denies murder, strangulation and GBH. The trial continues. https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text: Jensen Huang on a panel at the Microsoft Windows & Surface event in San Francisco in October. Photograph: Manuel Orbegozo/Reuters View image in fullscreen Jensen Huang on a panel at the Microsoft Windows & Surface event in San Francisco in October. Photograph: Manuel Orbegozo/Reuters Nvidia Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of action US commerce secretary faces sack as warnings emerge about alleged Chinese spy’s ties to Jensen Huang and delays in adding Megaspeed to trade blacklist Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached? Jonathan Yerushalmy , Mark Sweney and agencies Fri 13 Nov 2026 04.41 EST First published on Fri 13 Nov 2026 01.34 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google One of Donald Trump’s top lieutenants reportedly could soon be fired, as criticism mounts over commerce secretary Howard Lutnick’s apparent lack of action over the Nvidia spying scandal . Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday, and was replaced on an interim basis by chief financial officer, Colette Kress , after reports emerged of his multiple affairs, most importantly with Alice Huang (no relation), who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Pressure is mounting on Lutnick after it emerged that a US intelligence report about Huang’s relationship with the alleged spy was circulated among senior figures in the Trump administration . Lutnick is scheduled to testify alongside the ousted Nvidia chief before Congress in the coming weeks. He is also facing criticism for a delay by the commerce department in adding Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is associated with Alice Huang and has bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips in recent years, to Washington’s blacklist of companies that the US considers a risk to national security despite reported concerns within the administration. View image in fullscreen A screengrab from video footage by CTI shows Alice Huang (right), a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed, at a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan, on 22 May 2025. Photograph: CTI/AFPTV/AFP/Getty Images White House officials are now discussing whether Lutnick should be fired, the Associated Press reported. John Curtis, a Utah Republican senator, said that Lutnick’s reported delay on export controls regarding Megaspeed “raises the question of whether the commerce department is acting in the best interests of the American people”. Republican senator John Cornyn told the Financial Times there needed to be “a thorough investigation and accountability for the outrageous circumvention of national security export controls” and that: “Heads should roll.” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Jensen Huang and Nvidia must answer as to whether America’s security had been jeopardised, adding that the Trump administration also must account for what it did once it learned about his reported relationship with Alice Huang. “Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the banking committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News. A timeline of the affair scandal that sank Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Read more Trump’s close ties with Jensen Huang have also come under renewed scrutiny as a timeline of the saga started to emerge . The president called him two days before he stepped down and urged him to fight for his job, the New York Times has reported . On Thursday, Schumer questioned what Trump knew when he personally invited Jensen Huang aboard Air Force One on a state visit to Beijing earlier this year, adding: “Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships.” View image in fullscreen Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Photograph: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said he had demanded a classified briefing for all members of Congress about Nvidia. Republican Tim Scott, the Senate banking committee chair, said he had sent letters asking Lutnick and Jensen Huang to appear before him, because: “Recent reports raise serious ‌concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology.” Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached? Read more The statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal conduct revelations, instead paying tribute to his “profound” contributions to the company he cofounded. Huang is reported to have had relationships with Alice Huang as well as an Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, according to the New York Times, and another, unnamed employee, according to Reuters. House foreign affairs chair, Brian Mast, a Republican, said on Thursday that congressional staff had spoken to Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for Huang’s testimony. View image in fullscreen The Taiwan Stock Exchange opened 627.88 points higher at 43,719.75, with a turnover of 21.86bn New Taiwan dollars ($662.87m), amid uncertainty in the AI sector. Photograph: Ritchie B Tongo/EPA The House speaker, Mike Johnson, said on Thursday there was now growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China . Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company important to the US race against ​China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to ‌limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does ‌not want the Chinese military to benefit from them. “The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here,” Johnson told reporters ‌at the US Capitol, adding that he favoured limiting China’s access to the advanced technology. “I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.“ Chinese AI companies are now trying to secure Nvidia chip capacity outside China, amid growing concern that the gap in US export controls may now be closed after the scandal, people familiar with the matter told Reuters . Beijing has also stepped up efforts to develop domestic alternatives, including through Huawei, although analysts say Chinese chips remain less efficient for training advanced AI models. Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four bills on chip exports, according to statements issued since Monday. On Chinese social media, many expressed surprise at what they see as Huang’s swift resignation, and mourned the sudden end of an era that lasted for over three decades. News of his resignation attracted more than 400m posts overnight on Chinese microblogging platform Weibo. He had enjoyed rock-star status in China, where his visits drew crowds seeking selfies and autographs and his casual outings became social-media sensations. During a January 2026 visit, opportunistic sellers advertised photographs with him for 25,000 yuan ($3,700), while a Beijing restaurant launched a special menu costing more than 400 yuan after he ate there.
